author: fwyzard
body: #### PR description: Every module call copies the job's `ServiceToken` (a `std::shared_ptr`), or locks a `ServiceWeakToken` to it, and then releases it. This happens in `Path::runNextWorkerAsync`/`workerFinished`, in the worker tasks and in every `ServiceRegistry::Operate`. All threads of the job therefore update the same atomic reference count. On a large machine this cache line bounces between cores and sockets, and it becomes the bottleneck of the whole job. This PR adds `ServiceRegistry::OperateNonOwning`. It makes the services available on the current thread through a non-owning pointer, saving and restoring the previous context by move, without touching the reference count. `presentToken()` still returns an owning token. All asynchronous framework tasks now keep a reference or pointer to the caller's token instead of a copy or a `ServiceWeakToken`, and use `OperateNonOwning`: - the event path: `EventProcessor::processEventAsyncImpl`, `StreamSchedule` per-event tasks, `Path`, worker prefetch, acquire and run tasks, pre-prefetch selection; - transforms, workers without prefetching, stream and global transitions (`StreamSchedule`, `GlobalSchedule`); - the delayed reader (`DelayedReaderInputProductResolver`), EventSetup callbacks (`CallbackBase`, `CallbackExternalWork`, `ESProductResolverTemplate`), `SourceCoordinator`, and the run and lumi transitions in `EventProcessor`. This relies on the caller keeping the token alive until the asynchronous work it starts has finished. That already holds for the `EventProcessor`'s token, and for `SecondaryEventProvider`, which waits with `syncWait`. The once-per-job code (construction, `beginJob`/`endJob`, `writeProcessBlock`) still uses owning tokens. An alternative approach, winth one independent token (control block) per stream, gives the same throughput. It was not used because it only spreads the contention instead of removing it. ##### Measurements - **Hardware:** 2 AMD EPYC 9655 (96 cores per socket, SMT 2, 380 usable hardware threads in the container), CPU only. - **Software and input:** `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-11-1300`, the full HLT menu `/online/collisions/2026/2e34/v1.3/HLT/V2` running on CPUs only, on run 402360 HLTPhysics data. The input is read with `DAQSource` (`FRDPreUnpack`) from local FRD files. - **Job setup:** each job runs alone on the node, pinned with `taskset` to N physical cores and both of their SMT siblings, with threads = streams = 2N. - **Throughput:** measured by the `ThroughputService`, skipping the first 300 and the last 100 events. Job sizes go from 10400 to 49800 events, so that each measurement lasts at least 60 s. - **Clock normalisation:** the cpu clock of the job's cores is sampled every second from `/proc/cpuinfo`. The plots show the throughput normalised to a constant 3.2 GHz clock (throughput 3.2 GHz / mean measured clock), to separate scaling from frequency changes. - **Scan 1:** fill socket 0 first (1 to 95 cores), then add cores on socket 1 (up to 190 cores). - **Scan 2:** use n cores on each socket, for n = 1 to 95. | cores | before (ev/s) | after (ev/s) | |---|---|---| | 95, one socket | 380 (377 at 3.2 GHz) | 422 (445 at 3.2 GHz) | | 190, both sockets | 446 (379 at 3.2 GHz) | 769 (829 at 3.2 GHz) | Without this PR, throughput stops increasing at about 450 ev/s once more than about 110 cores are used, wherever they are. With this PR it scales almost linearly up to the full machine (89% of linear at 190 cores in scan 2, at a fixed clock). Up to about 48 cores the two versions are the same within 1-3%. The profile of a 190-core job (`perf stat`) confirms the cause: IPC goes from 0.73 to about 1.56 with the same number of instructions per event. With this PR the remaining `shared_ptr` reference counting takes less than 0.5% of the cycles, and the `FastTimerService` time not accounted by modules ("other") drops from about 470 to about 40 ms per event. ##### Not included: the transform interface The module-facing transform interface (`doTransformAsync` / `transformAsync_` in the `global`, `limited`, `one` and `stream` module base classes and their `implementors.h`) still takes a `ServiceWeakToken const&`. `WorkerT::implDoTransformAsync` now receives the token by reference and builds the `ServiceWeakToken` only at that call. The implementations ignore the argument anyway. Changing this signature to `ServiceToken const&` was tested, but the change is excluded in the current measurements to avoid rebuilding all modules. It will be included in the final version, for consistency and to remove the last weak-reference update per transform. #### PR validation: - All unit tests in `FWCore/Framework` and `FWCore/ServiceRegistry` pass (76/76). - The full HLT menu ran on 1 to 190 cores without errors.
title: Improve framework scalability above 100 cores
